summary:
LUNA-NAVI is an interactive, user-friendly application designed to support lunar landing site selection and mission planning, focusing in the landing of the Moon's south polar region.
Our project brings together NASA scientific data, lunar positioning calculations, and interactive visualizations to help users evaluate potential landing sites. It is designed to analyze Sun position, solar illumination conditions, Earth visibility, and potential communication opportunities across different locations and mission dates. A comparison feature allows users to assess multiple landing scenarios and identify important trade-offs between solar power availability and direct-to-Earth communication.
LUNA-NAVI addresses the challenge by transforming complex lunar environmental information into an accessible decision support using Streamlit interface. Instead of requiring users to navigate multiple technical tools, our application aims to present essential mission-planning information in one place.
This project is important because lighting and communication constraints directly influence lunar mission safety, operational efficiency, and landing site suitability. LUNA-NAVI aims to make lunar exploration planning more understandable for researchers, students, educators, and space enthusiasts.
details:
LUNA-NAVI — Explore the Moon. Analyze the Possibilities. Plan the Mission.

1. INTERACTIVE MISSION EXPLORATION

In LUNA-NAVI, users take on the role of lunar mission planners, exploring one of the most challenging environments for space exploration: the Moon's south polar region.

The journey begins at an interactive mission dashboard, where users can select potential lunar landing sites, enter geographical coordinates, and choose mission dates and times. From there, users explore five interconnected features:

(A) Mission Configuration — Plan Your Lunar Mission

Users configure their mission by selecting a landing location, latitude, longitude, and mission date. These inputs provide the foundation for evaluating the lunar environment. Picture shown below:

(B) Solar Analysis — Follow the Sun

Users investigate how the Sun's position changes at their selected landing site. Solar elevation and azimuth visualizations help explain illumination conditions and their potential implications for solar-powered lunar operations. Picture shown below:

(C) Communication Analysis — Stay Connected to Earth

This feature is designed to investigate Earth's position relative to the lunar horizon and identify potential direct-to-Earth communication opportunities. Users can explore why communication visibility is an essential consideration for mission planning. Picture shown below:

(D) Site Comparison — Compare Your Landing Site

Users compare candidate landing locations and mission scenarios, considering solar illumination and communication conditions. The objective is to support informed decision-making rather than simply identifying one universally perfect landing site.

(E) Mission Visualization — Explore Your Lunar Landing Site

The Mission Visualization feature allows users to explore their selected lunar landing site through an interactive visual representation of the Moon. Users can visualize the landing site's geographical location and surrounding lunar environment, gaining a clearer understanding of its position on the lunar surface.

2. PROBLEM-SOLVING AND CRITICAL THINKING

LUNA-NAVI encourages users to think like mission planners by exploring the relationship between landing location, mission timing, sunlight, and communication availability.

Users investigate important mission planning questions:

- Which landing location offers more favorable solar illumination conditions?

- How does changing the mission date affect the Sun's position?

- When might direct communication with Earth be geometrically possible?

- What trade-offs arise when comparing different landing sites?

- How can scientific evidence support a more informed landing site recommendation?

By exploring these questions, users develop scientific reasoning, analytical thinking, and decision-making skills. LUNA-NAVI emphasizes that lunar landing site suitability depends on multiple interacting factors rather than a single measurement.

3. KEY FEATURES AND INNOVATIVE ELEMENTS

Interactive Scientific Exploration

Users explore lunar mission scenarios by adjusting landing coordinates and mission dates, helping them understand how environmental conditions vary across the lunar surface.

Scientific Data Visualization

Interactive charts are designed to communicate solar elevation, solar azimuth, Earth visibility, and time-dependent mission conditions in a more accessible format.

Comparative Decision Support

LUNA-NAVI aims to bring multiple mission-planning considerations into a single interface, allowing users to compare alternative landing scenarios and understand important trade-offs.

Mission-Oriented User Experience

Rather than requiring users to interpret disconnected scientific datasets, the platform organizes information around a practical mission-planning workflow.

Accessible Learning Experience

The application is intended for students, educators, space enthusiasts, and aspiring researchers, including users without extensive experience in planetary science.

Expandable Modular Architecture

The platform is organized into separate functional modules, allowing the team to develop, test, and improve mission configuration, solar analysis, communication analysis, and site comparison independently.

4. TOOLS, PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES, AND SOFTWARE

LUNA-NAVI was developed through a collaborative software development approach using programming tools, scientific resources, and AI-assisted development.

Programming and Application Development

Python (Our primary programming language for application development, scientific calculations, data processing, and connecting different mission-analysis modules.)

Streamlit (Used to create LUNA-NAVI's interactive web-based dashboard, allowing users to navigate between mission-planning features and view scientific information.)

Visual Studio Code (Our main development environment for writing, organizing, testing, and debugging the application.)

Git and GitHub (Used for source-code management, collaborative development, branch management, and integrating contributions from different team members.)

Scientific and Data Analysis Technologies

NASA/JPL SPICE Toolkit and SpiceyPy

Selected as the scientific calculation framework for determining celestial positions using planetary ephemeris data. This supports the development of solar and Earth-position analysis at selected lunar locations and times.

NumPy and Pandas

Python libraries used or considered for numerical processing, time-series analysis, and organizing mission-related data.

Plotly

An interactive visualization library for displaying scientific charts, including solar elevation, azimuth, and other time-dependent mission information.

5. USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)

Our team incorporated Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a supporting tool throughout the development of LUNA-NAVI.

ChatGPT (OpenAI and Plus) and Gemini (OpenAI)

ChatGPT assisted our team with:

- Understanding the NASA challenge requirements and developing project concepts.

- Planning the application's architecture and defining functional modules.

- Providing Python and Streamlit coding guidance.

- Supporting debugging, troubleshooting, and software integration.

- Explaining scientific concepts such as solar elevation, azimuth, planetary ephemerides, and lunar mission constraints.

- Improving technical documentation, project descriptions, and presentation materials.

Other AI-Assisted Tools

Where applicable, additional AI tools may be used to support research, coding assistance, visual design, and technical problem-solving. Their specific contributions will be acknowledged based on the tools actually used.

Responsible AI Use and Scientific Verification

AI was used to accelerate learning, support development, and improve productivity, rather than replace scientific reasoning or independent evaluation.

Our team remains responsible for reviewing generated code, testing application functionality, and checking scientific interpretations against credible references, including NASA and JPL resources. AI-assisted code and data contributions will be acknowledged in project documentation. Any AI-generated visual or audio materials included in the final submission will be identified according to the NASA Space Apps Challenge requirements.

7. FACTORS CONSIDERED DURING DEVELOPMENT

Our team considered several essential scientific and technical factors.

Solar Illumination and Power Availability (The Sun's position influences the potential for solar energy generation and affects thermal conditions experienced by lunar equipment.)

Earth Visibility and Communication (The relative position of Earth affects whether direct-to-Earth communication may be geometrically possible at a selected lunar location.)

Landing Site Coordinates (Different locations, particularly near the lunar south pole, can experience significantly different illumination and visibility conditions.)

Mission Dates (The timing of a mission influence the environmental conditions that a spacecraft or lunar surface system may encounter.)

Lunar Terrain and Horizon Obstructions (Surrounding terrain can block sunlight or Earth visibility even when geometric calculations indicate that a celestial body is above an idealized horizon.)

Scientific Accuracy and Transparency (Our team prioritizes understandable calculations, reliable data sources, clearly stated assumptions, and transparent limitations.)

User Accessibility (The interface is designed to communicate technical information clearly to users with different levels of scientific and programming experience.)

Team Collaboration (A modular development approach allows team members to work on different application components while contributing to a shared GitHub repository.)

8. PROJECT GOALS AND INTENDED IMPACT

The main goal of LUNA-NAVI is to make lunar landing site analysis more accessible, interactive, and understandable. Ultimately, our vision is to make complex lunar science easier to explore and interpret.
